title: FADE: Mitigating Hallucinations by Reducing Language-Prior Dominance in Large Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2606.29431v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Despite the impressive capabilities of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), they remain susceptible to hallucination, generating content inconsistent with the input image. Recent studies attribute this to the dominance of language priors over visual inputs and employ contrastive decoding methods to mitigate this dominance, but the mechanistic origin remains unexplored. We investigate the information flow through each transformer layer and find that attention modules consistently aggregate visual evidence, while FFN modules at critical layers act as the source of language priors. These priors can override visual evidence, causing correct predictions in intermediate layers to drift toward incorrect outputs. Based on this insight, we propose FADE (FFN Attenuation for DEcoding), a training-free method that attenuates FFN outputs to reduce language-prior dominance. Evaluations on POPE, CHAIR, and MME benchmarks across LLaVA-1.5, mPLUG-Ow

translated_title: FADE：通过降低语言先验主导性来缓解大视觉语言模型的幻觉问题
translated_abstract: 尽管大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）具有令人印象深刻的能力，但它们仍然容易产生幻觉，即生成与输入图像不一致的内容。最近的研究将此归因于语言先验对视觉输入的主导地位，并采用对比解码方法来缓解这种主导性，但其机制起源仍未被探索。我们研究了信息在每个Transformer层中的流动，发现注意力模块持续聚合视觉证据，而关键层中的FFN模块则是语言先验的来源。这些先验可以覆盖视觉证据，导致中间层的正确预测漂移向错误的输出。基于这一洞察，我们提出了FADE（FFN Attenuation for DEcoding，解码时的FFN衰减），这是一种无需训练的方法，通过衰减FFN输出来降低语言先验的主导性。在LLaVA-1.5、mPLUG-Owl等模型上的POPE、CHAIR和MME基准测试评估表明了该方法的有效性。
tldr: 本文揭示了LVLM幻觉的机制来源——关键层的FFN模块产生的语言先验会覆盖注意力模块聚合的视觉证据，并提出无需训练的FADE方法，通过衰减FFN输出来有效缓解幻觉问题。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the mechanistic origin of LVLM hallucinations—FFN modules at critical layers produce language priors that override visual evidence aggregated by attention modules—and proposes FADE, a training-free method that mitigates hallucinations by attenuating FFN outputs.
